0.0.n: Used to open the talk and get listeners’ attention, rather than answer a question.

0.1.n: A casual greeting here, paired with はい as a friendly opening.

0.3.n: Addresses the audience; さん adds friendly respect.

0.4.n: A standard daytime greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

1.0.n: Refers to this installment or video, not necessarily today.

1.1.n: Marks 今回 as the topic, setting the scope of this talk.

1.3.n: Combines with 時代 to form the name of Japan’s Sengoku period.

1.4.n: Follows 戦国 to complete the historical period’s name.

1.5.n: Follows a noun to introduce the subject being discussed.

1.6.n: お話しする is a respectful way to say speak; ていきます presents the talk as unfolding from here.

2.0.n: Part of 戦国時代, the name of the historical period under discussion.

2.1.n: Combines with 戦国 to name a span of Japanese history.

2.2.n: Makes 戦国時代 the topic of the statement about uncertain dates.

2.3.n: 何 asks which year; paired with から, it refers to the starting date.

2.4.n: Marks the starting point of the time range.

2.5.n: Paired with まで, this asks about the ending date.

2.6.n: Marks the endpoint of the time range.

2.7.n: Marks the preceding year range as the content of what has not been settled.

2.9.n: Describes how definitively the dates are established; the following verb denies that they are.

2.10.n: Polite negative of 決まっている, describing the current unsettled state rather than an ongoing decision.

2.11.n: Connects this uncertainty to the practical date range chosen next.

3.0.n: Signals a provisional choice for the purposes of this explanation.

3.1.n: Points to the video currently being watched and must come before a noun.

3.2.n: Names the medium in which the speaker will use this definition.

3.3.n: Sets this video as the context where the chosen date range applies.

3.4.n: Added to で, it emphasizes this video’s scope, allowing for other definitions elsewhere.

3.6.n: 年 after a number labels a calendar year.

3.7.n: Links the year to the war, identifying when it occurred.

3.8.n: An era name used in the historical event name 応仁の乱.

3.9.n: Connects the era name 応仁 with 乱 to form the event’s name.

3.10.n: In historical names, 乱 refers to an uprising or conflict; 応仁の乱 is conventionally called the Ōnin War.

3.11.n: Marks the Ōnin War as the beginning of the selected period.

4.0.n: 年 marks a calendar year; に then places the expulsion at that time.

4.1.n: Marks the specific year when the expulsion took place.

4.2.n: A family name, placed before the given name 信長 in Japanese name order.

4.3.n: The given name of the historical figure Oda Nobunaga.

4.4.n: Identifies Oda Nobunaga as the person carrying out the expulsion.

4.5.n: A family name, placed before the given name 義昭.

4.6.n: The given name of the historical figure Ashikaga Yoshiaki.

4.7.n: Marks Ashikaga Yoshiaki as the person being expelled.

4.8.n: 追放 plus する forms a verb; this plain form before まで describes a historical endpoint, not a future event.

4.9.n: Makes the entire expulsion event the endpoint of the selected period.

4.10.n: Links the endpoint phrase to 約100年間 in the next line, describing that span.

5.0.n: 約 signals an estimate, while 年間 expresses a duration rather than a calendar year.

5.1.n: Marks the roughly hundred-year span as what the speaker will classify.

5.2.n: Combines with 時代 to give the historical label assigned to this span.

5.3.n: Completes 戦国時代, the name used for the chosen interval.

5.4.n: Marks the category under which the speaker treats the hundred-year span.

5.5.n: Polite form of 取り扱う; here it means classifying a period for this explanation, not physically handling something.

0.tip: はいどうも is a friendly opening, not a literal yes followed by thanks.

1.lit: This time, about the Warring States period, I will go on talking.
1.tip: Verb て-form plus いきます can show an activity proceeding from now onward.

2.lit: As for the Warring States period, from what year until what year is not firmly settled, but…
2.tip: 決まっていません describes a state: the dates are not settled.

3.lit: For now, in this video, from the Ōnin War of the year 1467…
3.tip: から opens a time range whose endpoint appears with まで in the next line.

4.lit: Of the span until Oda Nobunaga expels Ashikaga Yoshiaki in the year 1573…
4.tip: まで can follow a whole event description to mark when a period ends.

5.lit: We will treat approximately 100 years as the Warring States period.
5.tip: として marks the category or label assigned to something: treat A as B.
